meta.how_to_use: Each row is a decision, not a task. Read the evidence, pick one of the four statuses, and record it here before any code changes. The workflow on the Suggestions page is the order the review is meant to happen in.
meta.rule: No suggestion may be implemented while its status is 'pending'.

review_workflow.label: Triage
review_workflow.detail: Read the suggestion, its evidence and its cost. Nothing is implemented at this step.

review_workflow.label: Check the evidence
review_workflow.detail: Open the linked source and the referenced data file. A suggestion with an unverifiable claim is sent back, not approved.

review_workflow.label: Choose a path
review_workflow.detail: Accept, park, or reject. Exactly one path per suggestion, recorded in the register so the next session cannot silently reopen it.

review_workflow.label: Assign a gate
review_workflow.detail: Say which of the ten gates the change is meant to move. A change that moves no gate is parked.

review_workflow.label: Implement behind the gate
review_workflow.detail: Ship it with a check that fails if the gate regresses. No strategy page updates on an unapproved change.

review_workflow.label: Re-measure
review_workflow.detail: Re-run the pipeline and publish the new numbers, including the ones that got worse.

suggestions.title: Approve or reject the site's current answer before adding another model
suggestions.problem: The three sibling research builds in this repository disagree in places, and a reader cannot tell which verdict to act on: the root site says the closing market beats the model, the Skill Lab says 0 of 21 strategies qualify, the origination lab publishes a 2026 Week 9 slate that cannot be priced because no prop prices exist.
suggestions.proposal: Adopt one decision rule for the whole repository: a strategy is only worth building further once it passes the ten published gates on the committed extract, and no page may show a slate, an edge or a reward until it does.
suggestions.evidence: site/data/signals.json (0 of 23 variants pass), data/derived/leaderboard.json (0 of 9)
suggestions.source_text: evidence is recomputed from this feed on every run

suggestions.title: Timestamp every line, or stop calling any edge 'live'
suggestions.problem: The only line the repository holds is one closing number per game with no capture time. That makes Gate G1 - point-in-time integrity - impossible to satisfy, which is why every candidate in this session's lab fails at gate one regardless of its ROI.
suggestions.proposal: Add a capture job that writes (game_id, book, market, line, price, captured_utc) every N minutes into a committed append-only file, starting with the current week. Ten days of that is worth more than any new model, because it is the only way to measure closing-line value.
suggestions.risk: Medium - a licensed price source is needed; none is verified here
suggestions.source_text: the league calendar fixes when practice/game-status reports are filed, the anchor for a capture schedule

suggestions.title: Commit the injury, depth-chart and snap-count feeds on a runner
suggestions.problem: Injury and 2nd/3rd/4th-string depth work cannot be done from the sandbox: the release assets redirect to a host it cannot reach, and none of the three feeds is committed. The Injury & depth page therefore has 108 transcribed players and 108 blank 'which string' cells.
suggestions.proposal: Extend the existing data-pipeline workflow (which already downloads on GitHub-hosted runners) to fetch injuries_{season}, depth_charts_{season} and snap_counts_{season}, then commit a pruned weekly summary with the download timestamp. Handle the 2024->2025 depth-chart schema change explicitly.
suggestions.risk: Low - all three releases exist and are CC-BY-4.0
suggestions.evidence: site/data/injury_depth.json feeds F-1..F-4; nflreadr data dictionaries
suggestions.source_text: pos_rank is the only field that answers the 1st/2nd/3rd/4th-string question

suggestions.title: Fix the ATS coin-flip statistic before it is cited again
suggestions.problem: data/derived/luck.json reports n=13,784 ATS bets and a 50.0% cover rate with p=1.0. 13,784 is exactly twice 6,892 because every game contributes a cover on both sides, so the statistic is 50% by construction and the p-value means nothing. The conclusion ('no exploitable tilt') is still supported, but by the home-side rate of 48.91%, not by that number.
suggestions.proposal: Replace the pooled per-team-game rate with a one-sided home cover rate and report the exact binomial p.
suggestions.source_text: recomputable from spread_line, home_score and away_score

suggestions.title: Publish the parlay pricing gap as the headline, not correlation coefficients
suggestions.problem: The site leads with r = 0.561 between QB and WR1 yards. A reader cannot act on a correlation coefficient; they can act on 'a 2-leg same-team ticket priced independently is short by 38% on its fair price'.
suggestions.proposal: Lead with the measured joint-vs-product table, keep the coefficient as supporting detail, and state plainly that a house pricing legs independently takes an extra margin on correlated tickets.

suggestions.title: Give the leaderboard a reward rule that cannot be gamed by variance
suggestions.problem: 'Rewards for top performing strategies' is currently undefined, and a naive highest-ROI rule rewards the luckiest of many variants. With 23 variants tested here the best zero-skill per-bet Sharpe rises with the number of tries.
suggestions.proposal: Score on gates passed first, then on deflated Sharpe, with a minimum of 300 settled bets and a required positive lower bound. Pay nothing until a strategy clears all ten gates, and cap the number of variants a single entrant may submit.
suggestions.risk: Low - no money is held by this project
suggestions.evidence: site/data/signals.json meta.multiplicity and the G8 gate detail
suggestions.source_text: deflated Sharpe ratio: expected maximum Sharpe under the null

suggestions.title: Stop publishing a 'current slate' that the data cannot support
suggestions.problem: The committed extract ends 2026-11-01 while the official Week 10 injury report (games of 12-15 November) is already out. Any latest-week slate is a snapshot at best and stale at worst.
suggestions.proposal: Label every week-sensitive page with the data cut-off and hide anything after it.
suggestions.source_text: the official page is ahead of the committed extract

suggestions.title: Quantify what a starting QB absence is worth, before adding any other injury signal
suggestions.problem: Losing a starting QB is the one injury the market is known to move on, and this repository has never measured it. The backup-QB candidate in this session's lab returned ROI -13.9% over 208 bets, which is evidence that the naive version of the signal is already priced - but the sample is small and the rule was crude.
suggestions.proposal: Once SG-03 lands, estimate the line movement attributable to a QB change from timestamped prices, and only then build the in-game model. Expected value comes from the timing of the news, not from the fact of the injury.
suggestions.risk: Medium - needs SG-02 and SG-03 first
suggestions.recommend: Park until SG-02 and SG-03 are done
suggestions.source_text: the report is the input; the timestamp is what makes it tradeable

suggestions.title: Treat third-party feeds as third-party, in the UI
suggestions.problem: Several numbers rest on the nflverse mirror, which redistributes the NFL feed, and snap counts come from Pro Football Reference. The site sometimes reads as if the NFL itself published the number.
suggestions.proposal: Add a provenance tag to every table: official NFL / mirrored official feed / third-party. The same tag should appear on the source register page.
suggestions.source_text: nflreadr describes snap counts as provided by Pro Football Reference

suggestions.title: Add a leakage test to CI that fails on any future-dated feature
suggestions.problem: G1 fails structurally today, and nothing stops a future commit from quietly using a post-kickoff field. A gate that is only described in prose is not a gate.
suggestions.proposal: Add a CI check that every column used by a candidate rule is on an allow-list of pre-kickoff fields, and that every join is on a strictly earlier date.
suggestions.source_text: common pitfalls: data leakage in time-ordered problems

suggestions.title: Do not chase a profit until the hold is modelled
suggestions.problem: At -110 a bettor needs 52.381% of decided bets to break even; the repository quotes this but never shows what it implies for a 4-leg correlated ticket, where the house margin compounds.
suggestions.proposal: Publish the break-even rate beside every strategy ROI, and compute the effective hold on the measured joint prices rather than on independent multiplications.
suggestions.source_text: prices in the feed are used for settlement, not assumed

suggestions.title: Fund nothing, and say so, until there is a verified execution path
suggestions.problem: The brief asks for a leaderboard that pays rewards. No operator account, jurisdiction, limit, or licence has been verified here, and this repository cannot verify one.
suggestions.proposal: Keep every reward tier marked 'not funded'. Publish a one-page execution checklist (jurisdiction, age, licence, deposit limits, responsible-gambling links) that a human must complete before any capital is exposed.
suggestions.source_text: no official NFL page evidences a betting licence for this project
